description:
FOUNDATION (fact only, no behavior change). Classify every first-class callable value's CallConvention: Typed(arg_reprs, return_repr) when its RESOLUTIONS share one grounded uniform signature, else Boxed.

DE-RISKED: the convention comes from the RESOLUTIONS, not the value's stored type. The reducer's type is polymorphic (alpha,alpha)->alpha#31|#32, but its resolutions are concrete add_a@[int,int], add_b@[int,int] (already in CallableFlowFact.resolutions). Map each resolution to (arg reprs from its activation input types, return repr from its settled return type) via codegen_repr_for_lane semantics (int->RawInt, atom->RawAtom, float->RawF64, else->ValueRef). Typed iff all resolutions yield one identical (arg_reprs, return_repr); Boxed iff they diverge, or there are no concrete resolutions (genuinely opaque). This subsumes the phantom-surface concern from fz-rh2.29.7 (a Typed convention needs one concrete surface; retain_most_specific is its canonical input) AND the fault-3 'polymorphic return' concern (the convention's return is the resolution's grounded int, never alpha).

Record the convention on the callable's transport facts. PURE DERIVATION + telemetry; nothing consumes it yet.

CHECK: a focused test asserts the convention across the corpus -- reducer in opaque_fn_value_join and 00231 -> Typed[(RawInt,RawInt)->RawInt]; single-ref 00178 -> Typed; operator-ref 00181/00405 -> Typed; a genuinely heterogeneous/opaque callable -> Boxed; resource-destructor/provider-callback callables unaffected. cargo test --lib green, zero warnings.
title: Classify each first-class callable's calling convention as a transport fact
